newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Sterlite contests copper smelter shutdown.
newsitem.headline: India's Sterlite contests copper smelter shutdown.

text.p: Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd on Wednesday contested the shutdown of its copper smelter at the south-east Indian port of Tuticorin, which was ordered because of suspected gas emissions.

Authorities in southern Tamil Nadu state ordered the temporary closure of the 100,000 tonne smelter on Sunday, after more than 100 workers at a nearby dried flower factory were hospitalised. And a strike by local people in Tuticorin was held on Wednesday to call for the permanent shutdown of the smelter.
Anil Agarwal, chairman of Sterlite, said the company was not responsible for the toxic gas emissions.
"We'll now prove our innocence in the enquiry carried out by pollution control authorities," he said.
He said each day's closure cost the company 25 million rupees ($700,000).
Agarwal said none of the workers at other factories in the neighbourhood had complained.

"If such gases had emanated from our factory how is it that a thousand workers working in the same neighborhood did not feel a trace of it and only these women working in one of the three sheds of Ramesh Flowers were affected?" he said.
The workers, mostly women, complained of nausea, eyeburn and giddiness.

Hemant Jalan, chief executive officer of the Sterlite plant, said the symptoms shown by the women corresponded to those of chlorine gas poisoning. Jalan said no chlorine gas was used at the smelter, but added it was used in bleaching fresh flowers.
The copper smelter only came on stream five months ago and had been ensnared in controversy over pollution risks over sulphur dioxide emissions.
Two months ago protestors prevented a ship loaded with copper concentrate from discharging its cargo.
